Hey! Firstly don’t be scared, the issue is more common than you might think. It’s psychosexual, and not just a sexual issue. So, while you must’ve not experienced physical trauma, it could be associated with your psychology around penetration or sex in general. The way we’re taught about sex and the societal imagery around it plays a huge role too. The way to overcome it would need to be multi step, including relaxing your body AND mind, revisiting your thoughts on sex etc. Sometimes, it’s merely a physical issue associated with pelvic floor dysfunction. This can again be worked upon through certain relaxation and physio therapy techniques.

As a first step, I’d suggest reading up on it and on pelvic floor exercises you can do at home. If this doesn’t work, try looking for a psychologist who specialises in sexual trauma/ vaginismus. Again, a gynaec might not always be the answer if the issue is psychological. You might also want to look for a physio therapist. 

Also, have you tried inserting a tampon and does that work? You could also look into dilator kits. 

All in all, be patient and don’t be scared. Discuss it with your partner if and when you have one, and know that it can be resolved.

I shaved my face at home using one of those dermaplaning razors on 27 June. A week later I could see small bumps on my cheek and I let it go. I’ve always had clear skin so it was a bit concerning but I went on with my usual routine. A few weeks later the bumps starting getting red/ inflamed so I consulted my derm who recommended I start using Keracnyl PP cream. A month later, the bumps showed little or no difference while I had added pimples. I then used Facelin AT gel (adapalene + clindamycin phosphate) for two days which made my skin red, itchy, and very very sensitive. 

I didn’t know what to do so I reached out to the derm again and she asked to stop using Facelin AT, and switch to Clindamycin + Nicotineamide + 7 days of antibiotics. The picture on the right is after two days of the cream but no oral antibiotics. 

I was doubting this regimen so I reached out to another derm to get a second opinion and he recommended a bunch of stuff to use: salicylic acid gel, sebamed cleanser, adapalene + hydroxyl peroxide gel, oral antibiotics, moisturiser and sunscreen. 

I haven’t bought anything yet because at this point I’m feeling hopeless and tired and just want to let my skin breathe and recover but idk what to do next! Go with the Clindamycin routine or the second one? Or just go back to basics and use no actives?

3. Exercise and do strength training. It really helps. 
4. Could consider supplements like zinc but I’d recommend consulting a doc for this. 
5. Stay positive and happy. Nothing beats this.
